title: Rework routing decision eviction + introduce evented fallback supervisor
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: The current smart routing hotpath mixes synchronous policy evaluation, in-memory fallback queues, and coarse-grained regional locks. This arrangement causes long tail latency spikes under load, complicates rollout of new fallback strategies, and makes it difficult to reason about eviction/lease behavior across shards. Goal: Split the fast decision hotpath from fallback orchestration by introducing an evented fallback supervisor (EFS) coupled with a lightweight evaluator pool for the hotpath. Replace the in-process FIFO fallback queue with an append-only event stream that the EFS consumes; use lease-based shard ownership to ensure single-writer semantics for supervisor decisions. Outcomes we want: 1) Reduce lock contention and eliminate global mutexes on the hotpath. 2) Cut median and p95 routing latency for short requests by ~20-30%. 3) Make fallback behavior observable and replayable (event stream + compacted index). 4) Provide a safe incremental migration path with automatic canary to fallback supervisor and ability to revert to legacy queue without service restart. Implementation notes: - Hotpath evaluator: move synchronous policy checks (affinity, region affinity, tier gating) into a tiny, dependency-free worker that returns a stable decision object. Keep this path purely read-only with bounded CPU and no global locks. - Evented Fallback Supervisor (EFS): a separate service process that subscribes to the routing event stream (internal pub/sub). EFS owns complex fallback choreography: sitcoms like staged fallback (region -> tier -> model variant), circuit breaker resets, and cooldown timers. - Lease/ownership: use the existing shard lease mechanism (refactor to shorter heartbeat and async renewals) so only the elected supervisor for a shard acts on events. - Migration: dual-write events from the router to (a) legacy in-memory queue and (b) new event stream for a target shard set. Start EFS in read-only mode to compare decisions. After validation flip supervision via feature flag per-region. - Protobuf/IDL upgrade: upgrade routing protobufs to v3.2 to add the structured DecisionEvent envelope. Keep backwards compatibility by maintaining a translator in the router. - Observability: emit deterministic event ids and attach causal trace ids so we can correlate incoming requests, decision events, and downstream model calls. Add metrics: event processing latency, supervisor throughput, lease churn, event replays/sec, and decision divergence rate vs legacy queue. Rollout plan: 1) Spike and internal POC in staging (1 sprint): implement minimal EFS that reads events and logs decisions. 2) Shadow mode (2 sprints): dual-write + EFS in shadow; collect telemetry and correctness asserts; create regression evals using production traffic snapshot. 3) Canary (2 sprints): route a small percentage of shards to EFS-managed fallback; monitor SLOs and divergence; exercise rollback. 4) Gradual migration (4+ sprints): widen shard set, optimize supervisor logic, remove legacy queue when stable. Testing & validation: - Unit tests for DecisionEvent translation and lease semantics. - Integration tests with simulated surge traffic to validate no extra head-of-line blocking. - Chaos experiments: supervisor process kill/restart, event stream partitions, delayed lease renewals. - Golden-path regressions: compare outputs for 50k recorded requests against legacy logic. Rollback: feature-flag controlled; dual-write invariant preserves ability to fallback instantly to legacy queue. Telemetry & alerts: - Alert if decision divergence rate > 0.5% for 5m window. - Alert on supervisor lag > 500ms for 1m. - Budgeted rollout with manual gates at 25/50/75% shards. Risks & mitigations: - Risk: event stream backpressure could delay fallback decisions -> Mitigation: provide emergency sync-path TTL: if event not acked within 200ms, router uses last-known cached decision. - Risk: lease flapping during region failovers -> Mitigation: extend lease backoff and add leader-election jitter. - Risk: subtle bugs introduced via protobuf change -> Mitigation: translator shim + compatibility e2e tests. Artefacts and links: - RFC: https://docs.internal.redwood/rfcs/efs-routing-2025 - Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/2146 - Dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood/staging/routing-efs - Eval harness: gs://redwood-evals/routing/efs-shadow-v1 Note: this ticket focuses on the orchestration and migration; follow-on tickets will: (a) extract compacted event index for faster replays, (b) introduce an adaptive throttler in EFS to shape fallbacks, (c) migrate regional affinity policies into data-driven rulesets.
